citation.title: UDHF-SMERO: a unified deep hybrid framework for co-evolutionary smart material design and energy-adaptive structural optimizations
citation.authors: Rajesh M. Bhagat; Mangesh P. Bhorkar; Rajesh M. Dhoble; Buddharatna J. Godboley; Amar Jain; Hemant V. Hajare; Prashant B. Pande
citation.venue: Journal of Building Pathology and Rehabilitation 11, 165

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: The integrated framework takes about 0.82 seconds per sample against 0.34 seconds for traditional topology optimization, despite claims of improved performance elsewhere.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Section 4.4: 0.34 s classical time / 0.82 s framework time = 0.4146; the framework is about 2.4 times slower.
claim.alternatives: Abstract claims policy convergence under 100 episodes and adaptive performance of at least 95%; neither is directly compared there to a classical method.

baseline.classical_method: Traditional topology optimization models (Section 4.4); FEM solvers are also used as reference for structural response.
baseline.hardware_classical: Traditional models use 0.34 s; hardware not separately specified.
baseline.ml_time: 0.82 s per sample for full pipeline (Section 4.4)
baseline.training_time: not stated; Section 4.1 reports 200 epochs for Co-PIGT
baseline.data_generation_cost: not stated; Section 4.1 says datasets were partly synthesized and partly based on existing material-topology databases
baseline.quality_metric: Topology-to-performance R², energy dissipation error, inverse design accuracy, thermomechanical compliance, and prediction errors (Sections 4.1–4.2).
baseline.quality_gap: Section 4.2 claims baseline distortions above 8% versus below 3% for the proposed framework, without identifying the baseline implementation.

R1.evidence: Section 4.4 compares 0.82 s per sample with 0.34 s for traditional topology optimization; it does not match design quality or compare at equal time.

R2.evidence: Section 4.4 specifies an NVIDIA RTX-class GPU for the framework but does not identify the classical implementation or its hardware.

R3.evidence: Sections 4.1 and 4.4 give training epochs and sample inference time, but no training or data-generation cost and no amortization.

R4.evidence: Sections 4.1–4.2 use FEM models as ground truth and report prediction and compliance metrics, but do not report infeasible or failed returned designs.

reporting.n_test_cases: Static and sinusoidal loading profiles; Table 10 reports unseen design cases but does not give an overall count.

notes: Section 4.4 directly reports the integrated pipeline as slower than traditional topology optimization; the record retains inclusion because the article compares its computational cost with a classical TO method.
